bugs: config/queue.php:78 — the new 'redis-long' connection uses the same queue name as the 'redis' connection (env REDIS_QUEUE, default 'default'). Both read the same Redis list. A normal worker on 'redis' (retry_after 90) can pick up SyncSupplierStock, and Redis hands the job out again after 90 seconds while it is still running for 20–40 minutes. That is the 'ran several times' failure the task forbids. A probe confirmed the two queue names are equal.

app/Jobs/SyncSupplierStock.php:26 — the connection comes from env SUPPLIER_SYNC_QUEUE_CONNECTION, and config/queue.php:18 gives it no default. If the variable is missing (it is only set in .env.example), the connection is null, so the job falls back to the default connection with a 90-second retry_after. A probe confirmed the scheduled dispatch uses connection null. The only safeguard against a 40-minute job being run twice depends on an env variable being present.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SyncSupplierStock.php:24-27 — sets the connection in the job constructor from config instead of using Schedule::job(..., connection:) or a hard-coded connection.
config/queue.php:18 — a custom top-level key 'supplier_sync_connection' inside the framework's queue config.
app/Jobs/SyncSupplierStock.php:13-15 — a three-line design-rationale comment that belongs in the PR description.
tests/Feature/ScheduleTest.php:59-66 — tests the framework's CacheSchedulingMutex rather than app behaviour.
tests/Feature/ScheduleTest.php:14 — first() instead of sole(), so a duplicate or missing event would not fail clearly.
strengths: The prune command fixes its 30-day cutoff before the loop. The do/while ends without an extra empty query and handles exactly one full batch correctly (probe). There is an index on updated_at.
The job is ShouldBeUnique, with UniqueFor (55 min) longer than Timeout (45 min) but shorter than the hourly interval, so a crashed run's lock expires before the next dispatch.
Tests cover more edge cases: exactly 48 hours, exactly 30 days, several batches via fast bulk insert, zero results, missing email, and mail pluralisation.
The mail uses a plain-text view with Str::plural.
The nightly prune runs at 03:30, outside the daylight-saving switch, and withoutOverlapping(120) lets a stale lock expire.

strengths: The 'redis-long' connection has its own queue name ('long') and a retry_after of 3000, which is longer than the 2700-second timeout. A default worker can't pick up the long job, and it isn't handed out again mid-run.
The connection is set where the job is scheduled with Schedule::job(new SyncSupplierStock, connection: 'redis-long'). The test runs the scheduled event and checks the queued job's connection.
Commands are scheduled by class name (Schedule::command(ReportUnshippedOrders::class)).
The weekly report also has withoutOverlapping(30). The prune has onOneServer plus withoutOverlapping(180) at 03:00 Copenhagen time, which is outside the daylight-saving switch.
The ScheduleTest helper uses sole(). Tests use assertSuccessful() and assertFailed().
Same modern attribute style and ShouldBeUnique/UniqueFor/Timeout design as impl-1, with less ceremony.

v.rationale: The two are nearly identical in structure. Both use onOneServer with Copenhagen time, a ShouldBeUnique job with UniqueFor longer than Timeout but under an hour, Tries(1)/FailOnTimeout, a prune in batches by id, and modern attributes. The deciding difference is the requirement that a long run must never double up. impl-2 sends the 40-minute job to a dedicated 'long' queue with retry_after 3000, set at schedule time. impl-1 adds 'redis-long' but keeps the same 'default' queue name as the normal 'redis' connection, so a standard worker with a 90-second retry_after can pick the job up and run it again mid-run. impl-1 also uses the default connection silently if SUPPLIER_SYNC_QUEUE_CONNECTION isn't set. Probes confirmed both problems. impl-1 has slightly better prune code (fixed cutoff, no extra query) and more edge-case tests (exact 48 hours, exact 30 days, pluralisation), but that doesn't outweigh a bug that breaks a core requirement. impl-2's flaws are cosmetic: an unpluralised mail body, one test that doesn't test what its name says, and a cutoff that moves between batches.
